correction: An earlier version of this file claimed that opening the electrostatic loop would separate strands b7 and b8 and so unplug the attack site. Reading Souza et al. 2019 in full shows that is wrong. b7 (116-120) and b8 (143-148) are hydrogen-bonded strands of the same beta-sheet (Leu144 N to Val119 O); the EL is the LOOP between them and it hinges at residues 122 and 141, swinging away while the strands stay paired. What EL opening exposes is the metal site to water, which is what that paper measured. It does not separate the strands.
what_survives: Strand b7 carries, within six residues: Thr116 and Val118 whose gamma-methyls plug the Cys146 backside attack site, and His120 which is a copper ligand at 2.00 A, and then Glu121 leading straight into the EL hinge at 122. So the plug, a metal ligand and the loop hinge are on one strand. That is coupling along a strand, not strand separation, and it is a weaker but defensible claim.

supporting.molnar_2009: Souza ref 21: destabilisation of the electrostatic loop is reported as a property COMMON TO ALL studied ALS-associated SOD1 variants (J. Biol. Chem. 284:30965). That is what makes perturbation at the EL end of b7 relevant to ALS generally rather than to one mutation.
supporting.souza_qmmm: Closed EL has a more favourable enthalpy of Zn(II) binding by -99 kJ/mol (-23.7 kcal/mol); -T.dS about +15 kJ/mol. QM subsystem 590 atoms at HF-3c, with GFN0-xTB also used -- so xTB inside a QM/MM on SOD1 is precedent.
supporting.allosteric_path: G93A -> steric clash of A93 Cbeta with Leu38 backbone O -> T39, H43, K122, A123, A140, G141 -> the EL hinge. Mainly backbone-mediated.

revised_hypothesis: The cheapest route to unplugging the attack site is not backbone motion at all but a side-chain rotamer change of Thr116 and Val118. Their gamma-methyls sit 1.92 and 2.14 A from the attack point, and a chi1 rotation moves a gamma-methyl by several angstroms for a few kcal/mol. Whether b7 perturbation -- from EL destabilisation, from the copper site at His120, or from a mutation in the segment -- shifts those rotamers is the question worth asking.
how_to_test: Scan chi1 of Thr116 and Val118 and compute the attack-site occupancy at each rotamer, together with the torsional cost. Pure geometry plus a torsion scan on two side chains: cheap, needs no destabilised model, and gives the price of opening the site directly.
status: CORRECTED HYPOTHESIS. The structural facts are from the deposited record and from Souza et al. 2019 read in full. Nothing energetic is computed yet.
